title: TikTok Monetization
summary: TikTok has four main revenue streams: advertising, TikTok Shop, brand partnerships, and virtual gifts. Advertising is the largest stream, primarily through in-feed and TopView ads. TikTok Shop has seen the highest growth, monetizing through seller commissions and advertising fees. Brand partnerships involve high-value deals like hashtag challenges and takeovers, while virtual gifts involve TikTok taking a cut of transactions from user gifts.

key_points.text: TikTok has four main revenue streams, with advertising being the largest.
Advertising primarily through in-feed ads that appear every 2 to 3 videos in the For You Page, and TopView ads that take over the screen when users first open the app.
TikTok Shop has seen the highest growth over the past two years.
TikTok Shop monetizes in two ways: taking a commission on every transaction, typically 2-8% depending on category, and charging sellers to advertise their products on the platform.

Brand partnerships are premium, high-value deals like branded hashtag challenges where brands pay $150K-500K+, brand takeover days for exclusive daily placement, and large-scale brand awareness campaigns.
When users send gifts like roses or galaxies to creators during LIVE streams to show appreciation, TikTok takes a cut of those transactions before paying out creators.
TikTok Shop's growth shows they're successfully diversifying beyond pure advertising into commerce.
